title: Google Maps changed its default voice to be more 'natural.' People hate it
summary: The new voice for the directions feature on Google Maps started rolling out earlier this year as part of the tech giant's ongoing updates to improve the driving experience and make voice guidance…

image.caption: The new voice giving directions on Google Maps is part of the app's 'biggest navigation upgrade in over a decade,' Google said earlier this year. (Majid Asgaripour/West Asia News Agency/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

The new voice for the directions feature on Google Maps started rolling out earlier this year as part of the tech giant's ongoing updates to improve the driving experience and make voice guidance more natural with help from its Gemini chatbot models.
New voice for directions began rolling out earlier this year, tech giant confirms
It's been described as "angry and unfriendly," "an entitled know-it-all" and akin to "a snarky barista who wants to tell you how to live your life."

Google Maps has changed its default voice for directions — you know, the one that tells you where to turn and how many kilometres until the off-ramp — and it's safe to say many people are not fans of the new mouthpiece directing them from Point A to Point B.
"Why does my Google Maps default voice suddenly sound like a Mid-Western white woman?" someone wrote on X on Friday.
"The vocal fry kills me," a person commented on Reddit.
"I want directions to my next business meeting, not an effing latte," someone said in the Google Maps support forum.

In a statement to CBC News, Google explained the new voice started rolling out earlier this year as part of its ongoing updates to improve the driving experience and make voice guidance more natural with help from Gemini models.

blocks.text: Google started incorporating Gemini, its artificial intelligence chatbot, into its mapping applications in 2024.

There doesn't appear to be a formal announcement about the voice change on the company's website, other than a line within a larger March 2026 blog post saying it had "updated voice guidance to be more natural, like a friend navigating with you."
If the criticisms online are any indication, a lot people don't exactly think the new voice is friendly.
"She sounds like someone who wouldn't like me," someone wrote on X this week.
"Sounds kind of annoyed it has to give you directions," another person wrote on Reddit.

People generally don't like voice changes

Google launched Maps in 2005 as a desktop application advertised as a new solution to help people "get from point A to point B," the company explains in a blog post. It went mobile in 2007 (on Blackberry, followed by Android in 2008 and iOS in 2012) and added turn-by-turn instructions in 2009.
The new voice is part of its "biggest navigation upgrade in over a decade," Google explained in March, part of which includes more "natural directions."

In other words, as opposed to telling you turn left in 500 metres, the app will tell you to "'Go past this light. Then, at the next one, turn left onto Yonge Street,' in the new natural voice," Google told CBC News.

It's not the first time a corporate voice overhaul has triggered backlash. TikTok users hated the new text-to-speech voice when the company changed it in 2021, for instance, airing concerns it was "too excited," "too nice," and having too much "vocal fry."
Last year, iPhone users noticed "Siri doesn’t quite sound like Siri anymore," as Mashable noted. And there was downright outrage when Amazon recently updated its voice assistant, Alexa.

blocks.text: Some recent studies have suggested people can develop parasocial relationships or dependencies on some product models, especially AI chatbots, and changes to those models can lead to emotional distress.
But social media posts suggest the effect of changing the Google Maps voice may be slightly less deep.
"Why … did my Google Maps voice change to a woman who sounds pissed off???" someone wrote on X this week.
"She sounds mad at me," someone else commented.
